contests.title: Cherokee County schools — homestead value-growth exemption

provenance.sourceOrg: Office of the Governor of Georgia
provenance.quote: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from Cherokee County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes, through tax year 2031, in an amount equal to the amount by which the current year assessed value of a homestead exceeds its adjusted base year assessed value, provided that the base year assessed value of such homestead shall be adjusted annually by no more than 4 percent?

measures.questionText: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from Cherokee County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes, through tax year 2031, in an amount equal to the amount by which the current year assessed value of a homestead exceeds its adjusted base year assessed value, provided that the base year assessed value of such homestead shall be adjusted annually by no more than 4 percent?

provenance.sourceOrg: Office of the Governor of Georgia
provenance.quote: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from Cherokee County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes, through tax year 2031, in an amount equal to the amount by which the current year assessed value of a homestead exceeds its adjusted base year assessed value, provided that the base year assessed value of such homestead shall be adjusted annually by no more than 4 percent?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: For tax years 2027 through 2031, exempts the amount by which a qualifying homestead’s current assessed value exceeds its adjusted base-year assessed value from Cherokee County school-district property taxes, excluding school bond taxes. For the most recent owner, the base year is the tax year before the exemption is first granted; the tax commissioner would adjust that base-year assessed value annually by no more than 4%. The homestead must be the primary residence and no more than five contiguous surrounding acres. Improvements and added land would receive their own base year when added; removing land would adjust the base-year value and require recalculation, including final value determinations on appeal. A surviving spouse could continue receiving the exemption while occupying the home as a residence and homestead. It adds to other county-school-tax homestead exemptions and does not apply to state, city or county-purpose property taxes. The resident or an agent must apply to the county tax commissioner; the exemption then renews while the home remains the resident’s homestead, and recipients must report loss of eligibility.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the school-tax homestead value-growth exemption for 2027 through 2031 with annual base-value adjustments capped at 4%.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed school-tax homestead exemption.
